title: SOFR Daily Rate Observation – 2026-04-20
summary: The Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) recorded at 3.63% on April 20, 2026, down 2 basis points from 3.65% on April 17. Five-day observation range: 3.72% (April 15) to 3.63% (April 20). Source: FRED data series snapshot, no accompanying commentary or drivers provided.
key_points: SOFR recorded at 3.63% for April 20, 2026, a decline of 2 bps from 3.65% on April 17
Recent SOFR observations: April 20 (3.63%), April 17 (3.65%), April 16 (3.67%), April 15 (3.72%), April 14 (3.66%)
The April 20 print marks the lowest value in the recent 5-day observation window
Absolute change of -0.02 bps from the prior observation date
Direction classified as 'down' for the latest observation
SOFR is the primary reference rate for overnight secured lending in the U.S. money markets
why_it_matters: SOFR is the primary reference rate for U.S. money markets and serves as the foundational benchmark for dollar-denominated derivatives and loan agreements. Daily SOFR observations reflect conditions in the overnight secured funding market and inform understanding of short-term funding costs relative to the Fed funds target range. The current level of 3.63% sits below the upper bound of the Fed funds target range.
macro_context: SOFR at 3.63% reflects normal money market functioning. The 9 bps decline from the April 15 high of 3.72% suggests temporarily easier short-term funding conditions over the observation window. No policy decision or narrative context provided in source to explain the rate movement.
market_structure_context: SOFR is calculated by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York using tri-party repo data from BNY Mellon. The rate represents the cost of borrowing overnight cash collateralized by U.S. Treasury securities. Source is a 5-day snapshot with no longer-term series data or operational context (RRP balances, TGA flows) provided.
